tools.name: check_resume
tools.title: Check a resume
tools.description: Score a resume, optionally against a job posting: a 0-100 match score, the posting's keywords found and missing (matched literally, as an ATS search would), ATS format checks, the level fit, and the probability a recruiter would move it to interview.

job_description.description: The job posting to match against. Omit for a general resume check.

tools.name: compare_versions
tools.title: Compare two versions
tools.description: Which of two versions is stronger for a stated purpose. Asked twice with the order swapped and averaged, because the model favors the second option on close calls; if the two orders disagree the result is a tie.

question.description: e.g. 'Which opening line would an admissions reader find more compelling?'

context.description: The surrounding text, such as the whole essay or the job posting.

tools.name: grade_essay
tools.title: Grade an essay
tools.description: Grade one essay against a built-in rubric. kind "essay": six criteria and a letter grade, for class essays at middle school, high school or college level. kind "common-app": a Common App personal statement (pass the prompt number, 1-7). kind "sat": an SAT School Day essay, Reading/Analysis/Writing each 1-4 (pass the source passage to check quotations).

prompt.description: kind "common-app": which of the seven prompts. Default 7, topic of your choice.

tools.name: grade_with_rubric
tools.title: Grade against your own rubric
tools.description: Grade one or more submissions (up to 30, in parallel) against a rubric you supply: each criterion scored on a 3- to 6-point scale, summed per submission. Each submission is graded in its own call, so its score never depends on the others.

criteria.description: Rubric rows, e.g. { "name": "Evidence", "description": "Supports the claim with specific evidence" }.

tools.name: judge_choice
tools.title: Multiple-choice judgment
tools.description: Pick the option that best fits a text, with a probability for every option and a confidence. Options map an id to a description of when it applies.

tools.name: judge_score
tools.title: Rubric judgment
tools.description: Place a text on an ordered scale you define (lowest level first) and get the nearest level, the exact position and a probability for each level.

tools.name: judge_yes_no
tools.title: Yes/no judgment
tools.description: Ask any yes/no question about a text and get the probability that the answer is yes. Use for checks and gates, e.g. 'Does this reply answer the customer's question?'.

yes_means.description: What a yes looks like, if it helps to spell out.
